q8.answer: Staging is deduped to the highest updated_at per order_id, and the MERGE is guarded: a matched target row is updated only when staged updated_at >= target updated_at; unmatched rows are inserted. So an older or duplicate copy never overwrites a newer one, and a re-run rewrites identical data or nothing.

q9.answer: It is stored only in the warehouse table etl.pipeline_state (row orders_nightly, column high_water_mark). It is set to GREATEST(current HWM, window_hi) inside the same transaction as the merge, so it advances only at commit, after the night's data has loaded, and a replay of an old night cannot move it backwards.

q10.answer: Loading goes into the private etl.stg_orders table, which dashboards cannot read. The only write to analytics.orders is one warehouse transaction (merge, HWM update and status), so a night is visible fully at commit or not at all. The design assumes the warehouse supports a multi-statement transaction with MERGE, with an atomic table swap as the fallback.

q11.answer: The retry truncates staging at the start, so anything the failed attempt staged is discarded and replaced. It reuses the window_lo and window_hi stored in etl.runs for that night, so it extracts exactly the same window as the first attempt.

q12.answer: It re-reads all rows of each mismatched creation day (created_at::date) from the replica, not just changed rows. It loads them into staging, dedupes, and applies the same guarded MERGE in one transaction. It does not touch the nightly high-water mark, and it has its own etl.runs row with kind = recon.
